title: Pasta with Cream Sauce, Poultry, and Added Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with cream sauce, poultry and added vegetables is a dish that combines al dente pasta, a velvety cream sauce, pieces of chicken or turkey, and a mix of vegetables such as broccoli, carrots and bell pepper. The sauce is usually made from cream, butter and seasonings, giving the dish a smooth texture and rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cream sauces in Italian cuisine are often called “Alfredo,” although the original recipe differs from most modern versions.
The poultry is typically grilled or roasted beforehand to retain juiciness and aroma.
Added vegetables boost the nutritional value by providing vitamins, minerals and fiber.
Traditionally the dish is served hot, but in some regions it is served slightly cooled so the sauce clings better to the pasta.
It is popular in fast‑casual restaurants and family‑style menus because of its versatility and quick preparation.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Chicken or turkey supplies high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry provides B3, B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Vegetable nutrients
items.content: The vegetables add vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium, supporting immunity and blood‑pressure regulation.

items.title: Energy‑dense cream
items.content: Cream contributes fats that are a concentrated energy source and help absorb fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Complex carbs from pasta
items.content: Pasta offers complex carbohydrates that help maintain stable blood‑sugar levels when eaten in moderation.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The cream sauce and pasta make the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is important for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cream contains saturated fats, which can affect cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with dairy sensitivities should use alternative sauces.

items.title: Salt and sodium
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain added salt; those with hypertension should limit sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, tossing the pasta with the sauce so each strand is coated. Garnish with fresh herbs (parsley, basil) and grated Parmesan for extra flavor. For added texture, sprinkle toasted pine nuts or walnuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of cream or water to restore the sauce’s creaminess. Cream sauce kept separate from pasta can be refrigerated up to 5 days.
